test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Fitter) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Match the following.

 
 

 (A) Continuous thick lines
 (P) Projection lines
 
 

 (B) Hidden lines
 (Q) Principal lines
 
 

 (C) Outlines
 (R) Dotted lines
 
 

 (D) Extension lines
 (S) Object lines
solution:
__**Explanation:**__

 
• **(A) Continuous thick lines → (S) Object lines**

 Continuous thick lines are used to represent the visible outlines or edges of an object in a technical drawing. These lines are referred to as "object lines" because they depict the shape and structure of the object being represented. Object lines are the most fundamental lines in technical drawings, as they help in identifying the key features of the object.
 
• **(B) Hidden lines → (R) Dotted lines**

 Hidden lines are used to represent edges, surfaces, or parts of an object that are not directly visible in the current view of the drawing. These lines are drawn as a series of short dashes (dotted lines) and are essential for conveying the complete structure of the object, especially in complex designs.
 
• **(C) Outlines → (Q) Principal lines**

 Outlines or principal lines are used to define the main edges or boundaries of an object. These lines are typically continuous and help in emphasizing the overall shape and dimensions of the object. They serve as the primary reference for interpreting the drawing.
 
• **(D) Extension lines → (P) Projection lines**

 Extension lines, also known as projection lines, are used to extend the boundaries of an object to indicate dimensions or other reference points. These lines are usually thin and continuous and help in providing additional information without cluttering the main drawing.
